Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
247 of 2023 at Police Station-Kyoladia, District- Bareilly under Sections 376, 506 IPC.
The applicant is in jail since 26.11.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 06.03.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Rajesh Kumar Dubey, learned counsel assisted by Shri Mohit Kumar Gautam, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of Shani @ Ahmad Raza vs State Of U.P. on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117558986/

sentences.text: Delay in taking out proceedings under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. is fatal to the prosecution case in the facts and circumstances of this case 2.
The victim and the applicant were intimate.
3. The victim had eloped with the applicant to Prayagraj from Bareilly.
4. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship.

5. False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC against the applicant at the behest of her family members only to save the failing prosecution case.
6. As per the statements of the victim, the applicant was staying at her house.
The applicant had mixed some sedatives in the food which was consumed by the victim's family which rendered everybody unconscious.
The victim was driven in an unconscious state to Prayagraj.
The victim was staying with the applicant for 15 days.
7. Prosecution case lacks all credibility and is liable to be disbelieved.
8. No medical report corroborates intake of intoxicants/sedatives by the victim or her family members has not been produced.
9. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that the prosecution case against the applicant is false.
10. Major inconsistencies in the FIR, statements under Section 161 CrPC, Section 164 CrPC discredit the prosecution case.
11. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
12. The applicant has explained his criminal history.
It is contended that the applicant belongs to the economically poor strata of the society and is a convenient scapegoat for the police authorities.
The applicant has been falsely nominated in a case only to show the proficiency of the police investigators.
The said case does not have any bearing on the instant bail application.
13. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.

In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Shani @ Ahmad Raza be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Order Date :- 16.5.2024
